title: Waterfall, iterative and agile: what each one assumes about the world

videos.script: Somebody will ask you when the work will be ready. {{question}} Every software process is a way of answering that, and each one makes a bet. {{bet}} One bet says the requirements can be known before the work starts. So it plans everything first, and builds once. {{sequence}} The other bet says the requirements will move. So it builds a little, shows it, and plans again. {{loops}} Neither bet is foolish. The trouble starts when a team applies one to work that behaves like the other. {{mismatch}} This lesson reads the classic sequence, the iterative idea and the agile manifesto for what each one assumes. {{three}} Then it shows how much can really be known on the first day. And it ends with four questions for choosing a bet, piece of work by piece of work. {{choose}}
